items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Chu Berry was always there with Fletcher... I later joined Fletcher at the Grant Terrace... Chu Berry and Roy Eldridge and joined John Fletcher

ctx.x: At the Grant Terrace. Uh-huh. Great.

I later joined Fletcher at the Grant Terrace when our band broke up. I joined Fletcher; I took Israel Crosby with me. I took Roy Eldridge with me, and Chu Berry was always there with Fletcher, and we had another tenor saxophonist. He was a great saxophonist. He just died recently -- named Elmer Williams. He had a beautiful tone. This was during the time that Coleman Hawkins decided to accept Jack Hilton's offer in Europe and go to Europe. So Fletcher

had to get a combination of the two -- Chu Berry, who could swing, but didn't have the tone And all that Hawk had, but Elmer Williams had the tone, so he had to get the combination of the two together so he could play his arrangement, because everything Fletcher had was built around Hawkins in his arrangement.
Let's see. Now we're talking about 19 -- what did I say? -- 33 and 1934. These dates I have are later.
Now I have a thing here where Fletcher recorded Christopher Columbus on March 27, 1936, and he had personnel in his band like Roy Eldridge and Choo Berry, Buster Bailey.

Let's see. Here's the Connie's Inn orchestra. It's 1932. I guess that's Fletcher. Fletcher though -- Fletcher had been at Connie's Inn prior to your being there with Redmond, is that -- let's see -- December, 1932, Horace Henderson was playing with Fletcher, and you recorded "Honeysuckle Rose, New King Porter Stomp, Underneath the Harlem Moon, Yeah Man, Queer Notions, and so on. Those -- that goes on into -- that's all Fletcher's, but you were playing with Fletcher at that time too.
